newsitem.title: USA: U.S. group okays plan to improve transplant system.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group okays plan to improve transplant system.

text.p: The organisation that coordinates the U.S. organ transplant network Wednesday approved a new priority system for liver transplant patients.

The United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) said it voted to create a new transplant category, Status 2A, for patients with pre-existing liver disease whose need for a transplant suddenly becomes critical, putting them ahead of those without an immediate and critical need.

The more urgent Status 1 category of patients with sudden liver failure, children with a critical need for transplant, and patients needing an immediate re-transplant -- roughly four percent of all liver transplant patients -- would still receive first preference.
The number of patients listed in the newly approved Status 2A cateogry is expected to represent 10 percent of liver transplant patients, UNOS said.

"This new policy addresses the issue of how to raise the priority of the patient with pre-existing disease who suddenly become critical -- or 'crashes' -- without overlooking the needs of other critically ill patients...," UNOS President James Burdick, a transplant surgeon at Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore, said in a statement.

"These changes are about objective medical criteria for defining the sickest patients," he said. "This is an essential first step toward the transplant community's goal of broader sharing of organs for the sickest patients."
UNOS has faced criticism that its rules for organ allocation are unfair, and the Department of Health and Human Services is already rewriting the rules by which UNOS operates.

There was a huge public outcry last November after UNOS proposed changes to the Status 1 category, prompting fears that critics said would make it more difficult for some patients to get a life-saving liver.
UNOS also approved new pilot guidelines for matching donated kidneys and patients to increase the percentage of African-Americans and other minorities who get transplants.
